T-money is a rechargeable transit card sold at convenience stores (GS25, CU, 7-Eleven) and subway station kiosks for a small card fee.

1. It works on subway, city buses, and many taxis nationwide — tap in and tap out, transfers between subway and bus within the transfer window are discounted.
2. Balance and recharge are done with cash or card at convenience stores or station machines; unused balance can be partially refunded before leaving Korea.

Tourists spending over the minimum threshold at Tax Free-affiliated stores can reclaim VAT paid on purchases.

1. Ask for a Tax Free receipt/form at checkout, keep the item unused, and process the refund at airport kiosks (self-service or counter) before checking in your luggage if the item goes in checked baggage.
2. Refund percentage varies by amount spent; check the current threshold and rate before your trip since these are adjusted periodically.

Korea is generally very safe for tourists, with low violent crime rates even late at night in major cities.

1. Standard precautions still apply: watch for pickpockets in crowded markets, keep an eye on drinks in nightlife areas, and register with your home country's embassy notification service for real-time alerts during your stay.
2. Check your government's official travel advisory page for Korea shortly before departure, since regional notices can change.
